"REBUILD FROM SCRATCH: \"BLOX FRUITS 2D\", a complete, polished 2D pixel-art action RPG inspired by Blox Fruits. Single-file HTML5 Canvas, phone portrait first, joystick + buttons (keyboard too). Discard any previous version. Build everything fully: no placeholders, no bugs.

THE PLAYER CHARACTER (top priority: build this first and best)
Look: a young pirate swordsman, 32-bit pixel sprite about 48px tall, upright full body, readable on a phone. Strong silhouette: messy windblown hair, bandana with tails, open vest over a shirt, sash belt, trousers, boots, fingerless gloves, sword on the hip. Clean 1px dark outline, 3-tone shading per material (skin, cloth, leather, steel), one fixed light direction. The face is visible with eyes and eyebrows; expressions change (calm, angry when attacking, pained when hit).
View: ONE consistent angled GTA-style view shared by player, enemies, trees and houses. 4 directions (mirrored to 8), never seen from directly above. Y-sorted depth, soft oval shadow under the feet.
Animations (6-8 frames each, smooth easing, no popping): idle with breathing, weight shift and blinking; walk; run with forward lean and arm swing; jump with squash and stretch plus landing dust; dodge roll; block stance; hit flinch with white flash; knockback; death; victory pose; fruit-eating pose; pickup crouch.
Secondary motion: hair, bandana tails, vest and sash trail behind the movement with a slight delay. Footsteps kick dust on sand, splash in water, rustle grass, and leave wet prints on sand.
Sword: steel gradient blade, bright edge, guard and grip; drawn from the hip in combat, sheathed when idle. 3-hit combo with anticipation, strike, follow-through and recovery; the body rotates and the front foot steps in; fading afterimage trail along the real curved path; 70ms hit-stop, sparks, screen micro-shake, enemy knockback.
Fruit powers show on the body: eyes and hands glow in the fruit color, an aura of particles surrounds him, and the hair and outfit react (fire lights the hair, ice frosts the vest).
Extra life: a combat idle stance when enemies are near and a relaxed idle with random looks and stretches after 5 seconds. Low health makes him limp and breathe hard. Wading in water slows him with ripples and soaks his lower clothes. Customization: hair, vest and bandana colors with a live preview.
Stats: Level, Health, Energy, Melee, Sword, Defense, Fruit. A character screen with a large animated preview.

CAMERA AND CONTROLS
Camera locked on the player with smooth follow, player at 42% down the screen, never hidden under UI. Joystick bottom-left; buttons bottom-right in a spaced fan: ATK, JUMP, ROLL, BLOCK, S1, S2, ULT, semi-transparent, no overlaps. An Interact button appears near fruits.

WORLD AND ENEMIES
Starter island: village, forest, beach, docks. Detailed varied terrain (flowers, dirt paths, autotiled sand shore, animated water with foam, rocks, bushes), day and night. Enemies: bandits, marines, pirates, a boss per island, fully animated, surrounding the player at a radius. Waves escalate, a boss every 5th. Gold, XP, levels.

FRUITS
Realistic pixel Devil Fruits with swirl patterns drop in wave 1, bounce and glow. Interact, then Eat / Store / Equip; never eaten on contact. Each fruit: 2 skills, a basic attack, a 5-6 second cinematic ultimate. Real physics: fire spreads and ignites grass, ice freezes water and shatters enemies, lightning chains, magma pools and cools, rubber stretches and bounces.

UI
Start menu first (world paused behind it, no black flash). Crisp pixel font at integer scale, HUD without overlaps, inventory, fruit wheel, settings, pause, save/load, minimap.

QUALITY
60 FPS with object pooling. Test the player first: every animation plays, nothing is cut off, nothing is covered.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build and refine a polished, phone-first 2D pixel-art action RPG inspired by Blox Fruits as a standalone HTML5 Canvas game.
- Review gameplay and UI issues, make targeted fixes, and verify the game runs.

## Requirements
- Portrait-first mobile joystick and action buttons, with keyboard controls.
- Combat, fruit powers, customization, progression, HUD, inventory, map, settings, save/load, and pause.
- Start at the menu; avoid placeholders, overlap, and clipping.

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation in a single `index.html` with inline CSS/JavaScript, no external dependencies, and browser `localStorage` saves.
- Adapt the canvas height to the viewport in both portrait and landscape to avoid cropping.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game systems, menu, hand-drawn pixel art, combat, waves and bosses, Devil Fruits, progression, customization, inventory, map, settings, pause, and save/load.
- Fixed jump motion, held blocking, save/continue behavior, and starter-fruit persistence.
- Added a mobile menu height limit with internal scrolling, viewport-fitting canvas sizing, fruit-power cooldown, and ignored repeated keyboard keydown events.
- Validated extracted JavaScript with `node --check` and ran `git diff --check`.
- Captured portrait and landscape Chromium screenshots; smoke-tested start, settings, character preview, save, return-to-title, and continue. Smoke output reported all checks true and no runtime error.

### Active
- Review whether any additional gameplay, rendering, or mobile UI issues need fixes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the final diff and any remaining gameplay/rendering issues; make further changes only if warranted.
2. Repeat syntax and browser smoke checks after any additional edits.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete single-file game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is untracked in the current Git status.
- Browser screenshots and smoke-test copies are under `/tmp/opencode`; they are temporary and not source files.
